answer: One defense is to require every agent to lock a stake that is slashed on misbehavior. Forging a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, so an attacker pays linearly for each extra identity while an honest user pays once. Peer attestation sharpens this: like a prism splitting light, it separates genuine activity from duplicated patterns, since copies share timing and behavior fingerprints. A juniper hedge may look like many plants but shares one root, and a walnut shell protects a single kernel - cheap multiplicity is the attack, and a forfeitable cost per identity stops it.
